body.statement:
Assume \(p_0\in\operatorname{relint}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ASC}})\), \(\operatorname{im}(B)\subseteq\operatorname{lin}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ASC}}-p_0)\), the local-family affine-hull condition, multinomial interiority, base convergence, compact-uniform centered local expansion, effective moving-offset encoding, and \(c_n\to0\).  Let \(R_n^{\diamond}\) and \(M_n^{\diamond}\) be given by \(\text{def:comparison-window-schedule}\) and \(\text{def:windowed-multinomial-minimax}\).  These are diagonally selected expanding lawful windows; the stated compact-convergence assumptions do not assert that their selection is computable.  Then
\[
R_n^{\diamond}\to\infty,
\]
every finite atomic Gaussian dual certificate has a lawful multinomial realization inside \(B_{R_n^{\diamond}}\), and
\[
\lim_{n\to\infty}M_n^{\diamond}
=M_{\mathfrak G_0,\eta_0}(r_0),
\qquad
\liminf_{n\to\infty}M_n
\ge M_{\mathfrak G_0,\eta_0}(r_0).
\]
Conditional on the affirmative conclusion specified in \(\text{oeq:effective-compatible-density}\), or on a separately proved sufficient compatibility package, the Gaussian upper rules may be chosen from CertGluePFL receipts and their windowwise repairs are replayable whenever the needed finite-window comparison enclosures are supplied.  No conclusion about \(\limsup_nM_n\), no globally honest unbounded sampled-data primal, and no algorithm for selecting \(R_n^{\diamond}\) follow from the stated premises.
body.justification: The corrected theorem states the strongest valid result: global liminf and two-sided convergence on certified expanding windows.
body.gap: An explicit hard seam escaping to infinity disproves the omitted global upper implication.
body.consumer: It determines the exact sampled-data interpretation permitted for the Gaussian minimax certificate.
body.proof_tex:
\textbf{Technique: diagonal compact exhaustion, finite-support dual transfer, and exact windowwise repair.}

Write \(B_k=\{u:\|u\|_2\le k\}\).  Fix \(k\).  By \(\text{lem:compact-causal-domain}\), the relative-interior, affine-hull, base-convergence, and compact local-expansion premises imply
\[
B_k\subseteq\mathcal U_n
\tag{28}
\]
for all sufficiently large \(n\).  By \(\text{prop:carter-fixed-m-positive-cell}\),
\[
\min_{u\in B_k}\min_{j\in\mathcal J}p_{n,j}(u)\ge\kappa/2
\tag{29}
\]
eventually.  Zero-offset centering, the local expansion, and \(\text{lem:compact-moving-remainder-covariance}\) show that every comparison term in \(\mathscr E_n(\ell)\) tends to zero for each fixed \(\ell\le k\).  There are finitely many such \(\ell\), so (28)--(29) and
\(\mathscr E_n(\ell)\le1/\ell\) hold simultaneously for every \(1\le\ell\le k\) once \(n\) is large enough.  The diagonal definition then gives \(R_n^{\diamond}\ge k\), whence
\[
R_n^{\diamond}\longrightarrow\infty.
\tag{30}
\]
This is an existence argument based on eventual inequalities.  It supplies no algorithm for deciding those eventual indices or the compact suprema.

At \(k=R_n^{\diamond}\), the defining inequalities bound the Carter, covariance, offset, boundary, and finite-arrangement errors on the selected window by a deterministic number \(\rho_n\to0\).  The convergence follows because the accepted index tends to infinity by (30), while the diagonal tolerance at that index tends to zero.  This is the only moving-window comparison used below.

Let \(L<M_{\mathfrak G_0,\eta_0}(r_0)\).  By \(\text{thm:attainment-atomic-duality}\), there is a finite atomic Gaussian dual certificate \(\mu\) of value greater than \(L\).  Its finite support lies in some \(B_k\).  Zero-offset centering and \(\text{lem:finite-completed-arrangement-stability}\) realize each coverage atom in \(D_v^0\) by an atom in \(D_{n,v}\cap B_{k+1}\) at Mahalanobis distance tending to zero.  An equality-face atom is realized separately for each constraint role, and the completed convention retains its incident label.

For a risk atom \(h\in H_{r_0}\), the realization may be kept in \(H_{n,r_0}\).  If \(r_0>0\), the zero-offset cells are cones and distance to every rival cone is positively homogeneous.  Replace \(h\) by \((1+t_n)h\), where \(t_n\downarrow0\) slowly enough that the gained distance margin exceeds twice the directed Hausdorff error.  Arrangement stability then gives a finite-sample atom whose distance from every rival union is at least \(r_0\).  If \(r_0=0\), uniqueness of the label at \(h\) and closedness of the finite rival union give a strictly positive atom-specific distance, so the same conclusion holds once the arrangement error is smaller than half that distance.  By (30), every finite collection of these atoms lies in \(B_{R_n^{\diamond}}\) eventually.

Apply Carter's reverse parameter-independent kernel to an arbitrary window-honest multinomial rule, followed by the score and covariance maps.  By \(\text{lem:bounded-semantic-transfer-by-tv}\), the error in the finite dual objective is at most \(A_\mu\rho_n\), where \(A_\mu<\infty\) is the sum of the absolute dual coefficients.  Weak duality yields
\[
M_n^{\diamond}\ge L-A_\mu\rho_n.
\tag{31}
\]
First let \(n\to\infty\) and then \(L\uparrow M_{\mathfrak G_0,\eta_0}(r_0)\) to obtain
\[
\liminf_{n\to\infty}M_n^{\diamond}
\ge M_{\mathfrak G_0,\eta_0}(r_0).
\tag{32}
\]

For the opposite inequality, fix \(a>0\).  Attainment supplies a measurable \(K^a\in\mathcal C_{\eta_0}\) satisfying
\[
\sup_{h\in H_{r_0}}E_h\ell_0\{K^a(W_0)\}
\le M_{\mathfrak G_0,\eta_0}(r_0)+a.
\tag{33}
\]
Carter's forward kernel applies to every measurable randomized rule, so no finite representation is needed.  On \(B_{R_n^{\diamond}}\), the diagonal score, covariance, completed-arrangement, and boundary comparisons show that the transferred rule has coverage at least \(1-\eta_0-\rho_n\) and separated risk at most
\[
M_{\mathfrak G_0,\eta_0}(r_0)+a+\rho_n.
\tag{34}
\]
At the boundary of \(H_{r_0}\), (34) follows from the same explicit restoration used for the dual atoms.  For \(r_0>0\), radial dilation restores a deficit \(\gamma<r_0/2\) at displacement at most \(2R_n^{\diamond}\gamma/r_0\), a term included before the diagonal test accepts the window.  For \(r_0=0\), finite active-set chamber approximation and Gaussian-shift continuity supply the corresponding term.  Equality faces retain every coverage label.

Apply \(\text{lem:exact-coverage-repair}\) with coverage and risk restricted to the selected window.  With
\[
q_n=\frac{\rho_n}{\eta_0+\rho_n},
\tag{35}
\]
the denominator is positive because \(\eta_0>0\), and
\[
(1-q_n)(1-\eta_0-\rho_n)+q_n=1-\eta_0.
\tag{36}
\]
Since \(0\le\ell_0\le1\), the repaired rule belongs to the window-honest class and
\[
M_n^{\diamond}
\le M_{\mathfrak G_0,\eta_0}(r_0)+a+\rho_n
+\frac{\rho_n}{\eta_0+\rho_n}.
\tag{37}
\]
Let \(n\to\infty\), then \(a\downarrow0\), and combine (32) and (37):
\[
M_n^{\diamond}\longrightarrow M_{\mathfrak G_0,\eta_0}(r_0).
\tag{38}
\]

The globally honest class is contained in the window-honest class, and the global risk supremum is over a superset of the window risk domain.  Directly from the definitions,
\[
M_n\ge M_n^{\diamond}.
\tag{39}
\]
Equations (38)--(39) prove
\[
\liminf_{n\to\infty}M_n
\ge M_{\mathfrak G_0,\eta_0}(r_0).
\tag{40}
\]

If the affirmative effective-compatible-density conclusion, or a separate sufficient package, is supplied, the abstract \(K^a\) in (33) may be replaced by a CertGluePFL finite receipt; provided the finite-window comparison enclosures are also supplied, its Carter transfer and repair (35) are replayable.  This conditional statement does not make the diagonal selection in (30) computable.  Finally, \(\text{lem:escaping-boundary-kill}\) gives two arrays identical on every fixed compact but with different global upper behavior.  It rules out a global \(\limsup\) conclusion from the compact-uniform premises.
